To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BCL2 translocation is a strong prognostic indicator for germinal center type diffuse large B-cell (DLBCL) lymphoma.

(1) BCL2 translocation is associated with poor outcome in the germinal center B-cell subtype, irrespective of MYCH status; (2) BCL2 protein expression is associated with poor survival in the germinal centre B-cell subtype, and this is dependent on the BCL2 translocational status; and (3) double hit lymphomas, with combined BCL2 andMYC rearrangements, are associated with poor outcome

the prognostic impact of BCL2 translocation is restricted to germinal center subtype, that MYC rearrangments are rare, that the prognostics impact of MYC rearrangemnts is weaker, and that the prognostis impact of double-hit is stronger than that of single-hit.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the germinal center B-cell-like subtype of diffuse large B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma is not homogeneous and that the presence of isolated BCL2 rearrangement is associated with poor outcome.

the prognostic impact of isolated BCL2 rearrangement is limited to the germinal center type of lymphoma, but the presence or absence of BCL2 rearranged cases is not associated with outcome in the activated B-cell type of lymphoma.
BCL2 translocation is an independent prognostic factor for germinal center subtype DLBCL, and that the presence of BCL2 and/or MYC rearrangments is a very strong adverse factor for outcome.
